statement.p: The moment of inertia of a solid body about an axis in 3-space relates the angular acceleration about this axis to torque (force twisting the body). The moments of inertia about the coordinate axes of a body of constant density and mass m occupying a region W of volume V are defined to be I_x = \frac{m}{V}\int_W (y^2+z^2) \,dV\qquad I_y = \frac{m}{V}\int_W (x^2+z^2) \,dV\qquad I_z = \frac{m}{V}\int_W (x^2+y^2) \,dV
Use these definitions to find the moment of inertia about the z-axis of the rectangular solid of mass 32 given by 0 \le x \le 4, 0 \le y \le 2, 0 \le z \le 4.

static.solution:
V of the solid is 4 \cdot 2 \cdot 4 = 32. Thus for I_x we have I_x = \frac{32}{32}\int_W\, y^2 + z^2\,dV = 1\int_0^4\int_0^2\int_0^4\,y^2 + z^2\,dz\,dy\,dx. This is I_x = 1\int_0^4\int_0^2 y^2 z + \frac13 z^3\bigg|_{z=0}^{z=4} = 1\int_0^{4}\int_0^{2}\, 4 y^2 + \frac{64}{3}\, dy\,dx, or I_x = 1\int_0^4 \frac{32}{3} + \frac{128}{3}\, dx = \frac{640}{3}.
Similarly, I_y = \frac{1024}{3},\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad I_z = \frac{640}{3}.
